recipes.name: Hamburger Casserole
ingredients_raw: 1 (14.5 ounce) can peeled and diced tomatoes
1 (15 ounce) can whole kernel corn, drained

steps.text: Preheat oven to 250 degrees F (120 degrees C).
In a large skillet over medium heat, combine the ground beef, onion and celery and saute for 10 minutes, or until the meat is browned and the onion is tender. Drain the fat and set aside.

In a separate saucepan, cook noodles according to package directions. When cooked, drain the water and stir in the meat mixture, chili, tomatoes, corn, taco sauce, and taco seasoning mix. Mix well and place entire mixture into a 10x15-inch baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until thoroughly heated and bubbling, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Hamburger Casserole
raw_recipe.description: Taco sauce and taco seasoning mix give Mexican flavor to this beef and noodle casserole in which canned corn, tomatoes, and beans are included.

review.reviewBody: I think this is a great recipe. I used what I had. Skipped the corn and celery. Didn't have canned chili either. Here's what I did. Added garlic, celery salt, used homemade taco seasoning, chili powder and used rice instead of noodles. Made the rice, dumped everything else in the frying pan. Added the rice once it was done and put the whole thing in the oven. I have oven safe pots so I skipped the casserole dish. Also topped with cheddar cheese. Excellent dish!

I made this but incorporated a few changes based on other reviews. I added a tablespoon of minced garlic and put that in with the beef and onions. After I drained the fat, I added 1 teaspoon of chipotle Chili powder, taco seasoning with a bit of water, a few good splashes of Worcestershire sauce and two good splashes of Tabasco sauce. I added the taco sauce, 1 can of fire roasted diced tomatoes, 1 can of Chili, 1 can of corn,1 can of mushroom pieces and stems and used macaroni noodles instead of egg noodles. I topped it with an Italian cheese blend and crushed tortilla chips on top and baked it for 20 minutes at 350.

very easy to make. following other reviews, I added about 2 cups of Mexican shredded cheese, and 1/3 cup of taco sauce. I also added three cloves of garlic while browning the hamburger, onion and celery.
As we are trying to go gluten free, I used Bonza brand chickpea small pasta shells, and you truly cannot tell the difference in this casserole from regular wheat pasta.

Even with the taco seasoning and chili, I thought this casserole was pretty bland. I might make it again, but, next time, I would add the taco seasoning while browning the meat, onion and celery. I little salt and pepper might help too.

I also think 250 F is too cool. Better to bake it at 350 F for 20 minutes, I think. I made the recipe according to the directions and still had to heat plates in the microwave.

I added some shredded cheddar cheese to the top before baking. I think that was a good addition.

Not bad, just not great. Leftovers were gone the next day.

It was super delicious and crazy easy!! I did a few changes…I used about 1/2 cup of Salsa instead of the chili…I used a can of Rotel with green chilies instead of the Roma tomatoes and I mixed everything together on low heat and sprinkled in shredded cheddar and topped it with more cheese…also made my own taco seasoning…cumin, chili powder, garlic salt, and a dash of onion salt:) Huge new favorite of the family

I used chili style tomatoes instead of regular diced tomatoes, I also added a 1/2 cup of shredded nacho cheese blend and cooked at 350 degrees for 1/2 hour. It was so delicious i forgot to take a photo, but I will be making this often. My family is already asking me to make it again!

When I made my dish, I decided not to add the Mexican seasonings to this one. Instead I used my seasonings ( garlic pepper, parsley, seasoning/salt, pepper). I also added canned chopped tomato, minced garlic, oregano, freshly chopped celery & onion. I guess you could say that I made it with an Italian flair. I then topped it all off with shredded cheddar cheese. I also opted not to use the oven since it was already cooking on the stove top & it was an extremely hot summer day! I also used cooked macaroni instead of noodles for this one. It turned out Great! It was delicious as well as filling & nutritious.

This is a twist on another New England favorite, and what my mom referred to as "American Chop Suey". We had a hankering for Mexican food and there was a ~pound of homemade chili hiding out in the back of the fridge and we had (almost) all the other ingredients. Several reviewers felt inclined to omit and substitute, as did I. My chili was made with hamburger, so I cut the hamburger to 10 oz. We also substituted two freshly diced tomatoes for the canned. Otherwise, it was true to form. Our casserole was baked with a half-cup of shredded Mexican cheese and came out very good, but not great. One thing is for certain, we'll play around with this recipe again! This is honest-to-goodness comfort food made in a snap. I recommend fresh avocado as garnish and several shakes of your favorite hot sauce for the kicker. Yum! Serves up to 6.

Great base recipe. I altered it a bit based on what I had but the family loved it and we'll make it again. 

Instead of noodles I used large shells and I added garlic and bell pepper to the onion and celery blend. I also used half fresh ground beef and half leftover taco meat. Used chili seasoning instead of taco seasoning and stirred in a little leftover nacho cheese. Fiesta-style corn and fire roasted chili-style tomatoes for a little extra flavor. Once it was heated through I sprinkled the top with cheese and then returned it to the oven to melt. Delish!

I used macaroni , corn, black beans chili, and a chili packet and omitted celery because that’s that’s all I had in the house. I also used a mixture of Rotel and diced tomatoes along with the salsa. I bake it for 15 minutes and then added a 3 cheese blend on top and then baked it for another 5 minutes at 350 degrees

Pretty good stuff. Left out the beans, didn't have any. Didn't see the need to dirty another dish so mixed and heated on the stove then added noodles. I felt oven time may have made it dry. Tastes like homemade hamburger helper! I bet adding cheese then oven time would make it really good! Thanks for the recipe.
YUMMY!

One pot dinner! Boiled 8 oz of macaroni noodles (was a little too much); drained in colander & set aside. Cooked ground turkey & all other ingredients, then added the cooked macaroni. Skipped the oven, and just heated through on the stovetop. Next time I will use a can of Rotel for more flavor.
Can use rice noodles instead of egg noodles, kidney beans instead of chili. Double amount of tomatoes. Put cheese on top.

A great throw together meal when you don't have anything else. Doesn't take very long maybe 30 minutes to cook.Can substitute ingredients for what you have and still come out pretty satisfying. Filling, so your not hungry.
This is very good. Went by the recipe a little spicy. But this recipe was still good.
This was a hit with my husband , I also loved it… I only had frozen corn and used a bit more taco seasoning also covered in Mexican cheese… Next time I’m adding beans ❤️
I followed the recipe as written. Loved it. Right amount of spice without being too hot. Easy to put together. A definite keeper.
Really enjoyed this. As suggested, I added cheese on top (needs to be added to ingredients list). Next time I will mix two cups of shredded cheese into the dish instead of adding it on top. VERY good

When I make a recipe, I follow EXACTLY as stated so I can give an honest review. These people stating, I made exactly except I changed the entire recipe, can’t give an honest review. I made as stated and it was delicious. My family asked to make it again. Next time, I think I’ll make it with black beans and leave the celery out. It was a hit with the family!
